te.lib:h-nasab: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt or distress befalls a Muslim, even the prick of a thorn, except that Allah expiates some of his sins because of it.
te.lib:h-ashadd-bala: He was asked: “Which of the people are tried most severely?” He said: “The Prophets, then those nearest to them, then those nearest to them. A man is tried according to his religion…”
te.lib:h-azam-jaza: Indeed, greater reward comes with greater trial. And when Allah loves a people, He tests them; so whoever is content, for him is (Allah's) pleasure, and whoever is discontent, for him is (Allah's) displeasure.
te.lib:h-maradh-kutib: When a servant falls ill or travels, the like of what he used to do when at home and in good health is recorded for him.
te.lib:h-dawa: Allah has not sent down a disease except that He has also sent down its cure.
te.lib:h-tadawaw: Seek medical treatment, for Allah has not made a disease without appointing a remedy for it, except for one disease: old age.
te.lib:h-habibatayn: Allah said: “If I afflict My servant in his two beloved things and he is patient, I will compensate him for them with Paradise” — meaning his eyes.
te.lib:h-la-yatamanna: None of you should wish for death because of a harm that has befallen him. If he must do so, let him say: “O Allah, keep me alive as long as life is better for me, and take my life when death is better for me.”
te.lib:h-yurid-khayran: When Allah wants good for someone, He afflicts him with trials.
te.lib:h-sabr-diya: …Prayer is light, charity is proof, and patience is illumination…
te.lib:h-yatasabbar: Whoever strives to be patient, Allah will make him patient. And no one has been given a gift better and more vast than patience.
te.lib:h-hamm: O Allah, I seek refuge with You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from the burden of debt and from being overpowered by men.
te.lib:h-karb: There is no god but Allah, the Mighty, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Noble Throne.
te.lib:h-dhunnun: The supplication of Dhun-Nun (Yunus) when he supplicated in the belly of the whale was: “There is no god but You, glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers.” No Muslim man ever supplicates with it for anything except that Allah responds to him.
te.lib:h-abduk: No one is ever afflicted with worry or grief and says: “O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant, the son of Your maidservant; my forelock is in Your hand; Your judgement upon me is assured, and Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every name that is Yours… to make the Quran the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the remover of my sadness and the reliever of my distress,” except that Allah removes his worry and grief and replaces it with relief.
te.lib:h-rahmataka: The supplications of the distressed: “O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for, so do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye, and set right all my affairs. There is no god but You.”
te.lib:h-hasbuna: “Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs” — Ibrahim said it when he was thrown into the fire, and Muhammad ﷺ said it when they said: “The people have gathered against you, so fear them.”
te.lib:h-bismillah-yadurr: Whoever says three times: “In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,” no sudden affliction will befall him until the morning…
te.lib:h-ruqya-alam: Place your hand on the part of your body that hurts and say “Bismillah” (in the name of Allah) three times, and say seven times: “I seek refuge with Allah and His power from the evil of what I feel and what I fear.”
te.lib:h-adhhib-bas: O Allah, Lord of mankind, remove the harm and heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing — a healing that leaves no illness behind.
te.lib:h-la-bas: When the Prophet ﷺ visited a sick person he would say: “No harm; it is a purification, if Allah wills.”
te.lib:h-barrakt: Why would one of you kill his brother? If you see something that you like, why did you not pray for blessing for him?
te.lib:h-muawwidhat: Have you not seen the verses revealed tonight, the like of which has never been seen? “Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak” and “Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind.”
te.lib:h-uidhukuma: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek protection for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, saying: “I seek protection for you both in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every poisonous creature, and from every evil eye.”
te.lib:h-khattaun: Every son of Adam sins, and the best of those who sin are those who repent.
te.lib:h-farah-tawba: Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant when he turns to Him than one of you who was on his mount in a waterless desert, and it ran away from him carrying his food and drink, and he lost all hope of it… Then, while he was in that state, there it was, standing before him. He took hold of its reins and said out of extreme joy: “O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your Lord” — he erred out of extreme joy.
te.lib:h-yabsut-yadah: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, stretches out His hand at night so that the one who sinned during the day may repent, and stretches out His hand during the day so that the one who sinned at night may repent — until the sun rises from the west.
te.lib:h-ma-daawtani: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “O son of Adam, as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for what you have done, and I do not mind. O son of Adam, were your sins to reach the clouds of the sky and you then sought My forgiveness, I would forgive you, and I do not mind…”
te.lib:h-sayyid-istighfar: The best way of seeking forgiveness is to say: “O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I hold to Your covenant and promise as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.”
te.lib:h-atbi-sayyia: Fear Allah wherever you are, follow a bad deed with a good one and it will wipe it out, and treat people with good character.
te.lib:h-qatil-mia: Among those before you was a man who killed ninety-nine people… The scholar said: “Who stands between him and repentance? Go to such and such a land, for there are people there who worship Allah; worship Allah with them, and do not return to your land, for it is an evil land…”
te.lib:h-waswasa-sarih: Some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ came and asked him: “We find in ourselves thoughts that each of us considers too grave to utter.” He said: “Do you really find that?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “That is clear faith.”
te.lib:h-tajawaz: Allah has pardoned my Ummah for what occurs to their minds, as long as they do not act upon it or speak of it.
te.lib:h-waswasa-intahi: Satan comes to one of you and says: “Who created this? Who created that?” until he says: “Who created your Lord?” When it reaches that, let him seek refuge with Allah and stop.
te.lib:h-muqallib: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would often say: “O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.”
te.lib:h-ahdini: Say: “O Allah, guide me and keep me on the right course.”
te.lib:h-taqwaha: O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it, for You are the best to purify it; You are its Protector and Guardian.
te.lib:h-kfini-halal: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and make me independent by Your bounty of all besides You.
te.lib:h-la-sahl: O Allah, nothing is easy except what You make easy, and You make the difficult easy if You will.
te.lib:h-zawal-nima: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the loss of Your blessing, the change of Your protection, the suddenness of Your punishment, and all Your displeasure.
te.lib:h-istijaba-ajal: The supplication of any of you is answered as long as he is not hasty and says: “I supplicated but I was not answered.”
te.lib:h-nuzul: Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, saying: “Who is calling upon Me, that I may answer him? Who is asking of Me, that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?”
te.lib:h-sujud: The nearest a servant comes to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so make plenty of supplication.
te.lib:h-hazabahu: Whenever a matter distressed the Prophet ﷺ, he prayed.
te.lib:h-arihna: O Bilal, call the iqamah for prayer; give us rest through it.
te.lib:h-din-yusr: Religion is ease, and no one makes religion too hard for himself except that it overcomes him. So aim for what is right, come as close to it as you can, and receive glad tidings.
